title: Teaching Gurmukhi
hookLine: the first letters, taught at home or in weekend school
tomorrow: Fateh's sleeping over and won't settle. which story will work?

lines: FEEL A LETTER BEFORE YOU READ IT.
cards: Before a kid can read a letter, they can feel one. That's why alphabet toys come in wood and foam you can hold.
This Sunday Simran is covering the youngest Punjabi class at the gurdwara: a row of five-year-olds, a stack of worksheets, and one boy in the front sliding off his chair.
Sehaj's name is on the board, because everyone's heard about the new baby, and it starts with sassa. So Simran tries something Bebe once did for her.
She turns the boy's hand palm up and draws on it with one finger, slowly. A curl. A hook.

teach.b: Gurmukhi is the script the Guru Granth Sahib is written in. Sikh families teach it at home and in weekend classes like this one, so that children can one day read the Granth for themselves, not only hear it.
And the Granth treats letters as teachers. On ang 432 is Guru Nanak's Patti, named for the writing board a child learned on.

It walks through the letters one by one, and each letter opens a line about God. It begins with sassa, the very letter on Simran's board. In paraphrase: the One who made the world is the one Master of all.
The hymn's frame is a schoolroom, and its refrain turns the lesson around. In paraphrase again: why forget, foolish mind?
You'll be called learned when you can account for how you've lived. Here's something to tell a friend tonight.
Look closely at Ik Onkar, the symbol that opens the Granth. After the numeral one sits the curling letter ura, with a long line sweeping over the top.
The letters children trace are already inside the first mark of the scripture. So teaching Gurmukhi is two lessons at once: the shape in the hand, and the life the letters point at.

how: Sikh children learn Gurmukhi at home and in weekend classes at the gurdwara, starting with the letters and moving toward reading Gurbani for themselves.

games.q: your niece won't sit for her alphabet worksheet. going by today, what's the move?
o: make her copy the whole row until she gets it right.
trace the letter on her palm so she feels its shape first.
skip the letters and play her kirtan till she learns by ear.
games.why: a letter can be felt before it's read. Simran drew sassa on a wiggly five-year-old's palm, and he asked for it again.

practice: Turn one hand palm up. With a finger of the other, slowly draw the first letter of your own name, in any script you know.
Draw it three times, feeling where the line bends, then let your hands rest and keep the shape in mind for the sit.

wordCard.voice: Teaching Gurmukhi. Passing on the Granth's script, letter by letter, so a child can one day read it alone.
